one_month_reasoning: Two scheduled events fall inside the window. (1) Q3 2026 earnings: the date is still not on the IR calendar as of 2026-10-02 and no 8-K has announced it (EDGAR filing index), but the Oct 31 2024 / Oct 30 2025 pattern and vendor estimates of ~Oct 29 put it about 85-90% inside the window, which ends Fri Oct 30 (up from my 75%). (2) FOMC on Oct 27-28, following the Sep 16 hike to 3.75-4.00%, where the statement says inflation remains elevated. Quanta has beaten and raised every quarter in 2026 (guide went from $12.65-13.35 to $16.45-16.95), and backlog is +49% YoY, so another beat is likely. But consensus has moved up to ~$4.99, and earnings-day reactions run in both directions (+17.3% on Jul 30, 2026; about -2.5% after Q3-25). A second Fed hike would hit a 34x stock. Together these give no reliable directional edge. I keep a near-symmetric distribution: median about $664 against $662.60 for a tiny beat-and-raise tilt, and one-month sigma about 13.5%, a little above plain 44%/3.5 = 12.6% because two binary events land in the window.

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (NTM EPS at Oct-2027 of ~$21.9 x 30x = $658, weight 0.5), FCF yield (2028E FCF $3.1B at 3.1% over ~152M shares = $658, weight 0.25) and EV/EBITDA (NTM EBITDA ~$5.3B x 19.5x less ~$5.6B net debt over ~152M shares = $643, weight 0.25). Blended about $655, down from $675 because multiples are a turn lower after the Sep 16 Fed hike. A slightly higher 2028 EPS (stronger backlog) and lower net debt only partly offset that.

inputs_detail.derivation: Yahoo consensus is $19.64 from 25 analysts. That is about +17.5% on the $16.70 guide midpoint and fits record 12-month backlog of $32.3B (Q2 revenue run-rate ~$38B) and acquisitions contributing a full year.

2027E grown about 16%. That is slightly above the Street's ~15% long-run EPS CAGR (TIKR/Bernstein) because total backlog is +49% YoY ($35.85B to $53.44B) and 12-month backlog is +61% ($20.0B to $32.3B) per the Q2 8-K backlog table, with most of the NiSource program still excluded (ops commentary). Investor Day 2030 targets ($21.60-26.75) look conservative.

Today about 34x 2027 consensus ($662.6/$19.64), down from ~50x in June (TIKR, Sep 24). In round 1 I used 31x. I cut a further turn because the Fed raised the funds rate to 3.75-4.00% on Sep 16, 2026 and the statement says inflation remains elevated, so a 4%+ policy rate argues against high-30s multiples for long-duration growth. 30x on Oct-2027 NTM EPS still keeps a premium over peers and pre-2023 levels of ~23x, justified by the 25% 10-year EPS CAGR and 12-15% ROIC targets. Stress test: at 27x the method gives ~$591, and at 33x ~$723.
2026 guide midpoint $4.15B grown about 15% a year for two years, in line with EPS growth and margins holding near 10.5% (Investor Day target band 10-11%).
$5.5B x ~56% conversion (between the 53% in 2026E and the 55-60% 2030 target).

FCF yield on 2026 guidance is about 2.3% at a ~$100B market cap. In round 1 I normalized to 3.0% as growth slows. I now use 3.1% because higher policy rates after the Sep 16 hike to 3.75-4.00% raise the required yield.

150.34M basic outstanding on 7/27/26, 152.4M Q2 weighted diluted, and a 2026 guide of 152.5M. No buybacks in H1 2026 against the $1.0B authorization, and acquisitions are partly share-settled, so I use ~152M (round 1: 151M).

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: NTM EBITDA at Oct-2027 ~$5.3B x 19.5x = $103.4B EV less ~$5.6B net debt / ~152M shares

inputs_detail.derivation: Blend of ~$4.8B 2027E and ~$5.5B 2028E, each built from the 2026 guide midpoint of $4.15B at about +15% a year.

Current EV is about $106B ($99.8B market cap plus ~$5.9B net debt), about 25.5x 2026E and 22x 2027E EBITDA. I assume ~2.5x compression by Oct-2027 (round 1: 2x). The extra half turn reflects the Sep 16 Fed hike, consistent with the P/E method.

424B5 capitalization table at 6/30/26: cash $506M to $1,400M as adjusted, total debt $6,105M to $6,998M, so pro forma net debt is ~$5.6B. The notes repaid CP and the revolver and did not raise net debt. CP then rose to ~$728M by Jul 30 (424B5 footnote), mostly the July Enerfab payment (ops commentary: four acquisitions, $1.24B upfront), which puts current net debt at ~$5.9B. Over 12 months, ~$2.6B of FCF less ~$2.0B of M&A, earnouts and dividends leaves ~$5.6B at Oct-2027. That is lower than my round-1 $6.0B but not the $5.0B some assumed.

bear.story: Rates and AI-capex digestion together: the Fed hikes again, hyperscalers slow 2027 capex toward the low end of the ~25% consensus, and Texas-style permitting pauses spread. Direct Technology & Load Centers exposure is only ~10% of revenue, so the EPS hit is moderate (2027 ~$18.5-19), but the multiple derates to ~23x, the peer/pre-2023 level. That gives about $440, near the 52-week low of $404.

base.story: 2027 adj EPS of ~$19.6-20 on a 61%-larger 12-month backlog, with NiSource entering backlog through H2 2026 and Electric margins near 10.5-11%. The forward multiple compresses to ~30-31x on ~$22 NTM EPS as higher rates cap valuations. That gives about $690.

bull.story: Another beat-and-raise year: 2027 EPS ~$21+, 765kV transmission and generation awards stack early, 2030 targets are raised, and the Fed pauses after one more hike so the multiple holds ~35-36x on ~$26 NTM EPS. That gives about $940.

thesis_break_reason: $440 is about 34% below spot and ~22.5x 2027 consensus EPS ($19.64), near the peer/pre-2023 multiple of ~23x, and just above the $404.51 52-week low. At 44% vol a 1-sigma down year reaches ~$430-450, so a move there more likely reflects a fundamental break than drift: a guidance cut, a sequential backlog decline (backlog is +49% YoY now), NiSource or other large programs slipping out of 2027, a large fixed-price loss, or a broad hyperscaler/utility capex pullback. I keep this a little below the supervisor's $455 because a rates-driven derating to ~24x alone (no fundamental break) would reach about $470.

reasoning: Round 2. The primary-document base is unchanged: the Q2-26 8-K and ops commentary, the 10-Q, the 424B5, the Investor Day deck and the call transcript. The supervisor's findings, checked against primary sources, change three things. (a) Rates: the FOMC statement confirms a 25bp hike to 3.75-4.00% on Sep 16 with inflation still elevated, which I had ignored. I cut the target P/E from 31x to 30x, the EV/EBITDA multiple from 20x to 19.5x and raised the required FCF yield from 3.0% to 3.1%. (b) Net debt: the 424B5 capitalization table shows pro forma cash of $1.4B, so the notes left net debt at ~$5.6B; the July Enerfab payment (CP $728M by Jul 30) lifts it to ~$5.9B now and ~$5.6B by Oct-2027. That adds ~$3/share. (c) Backlog is +49% YoY (12-month +61%) per the 8-K table, and direct data-center exposure is ~10% (confirmed in the ops-commentary end-market table). That supports a slightly higher 2028 EPS (~$22.7) and a somewhat lower crash weight from data-center policy, offset by the new Texas permit halt (confirmed on the governor's site) as a catalyst. Net effect: fair value $675 to $655, with all three methods at $643-658. The scenario-weighted value is ~$697 (bear $440/22%, base $690/53%, bull $940/25%). The ladder is a lognormal with median ~$668 (round 1: $680), pulled toward the fair value because of the rates headwind, with sigma ~0.41 and a slightly fat far-left tail. That gives P(>= $663) = 0.51 and P(>= $895) = 0.24. Research added 6 fetches, all primary (EDGAR index, 8-Ks, 424B5, ops commentary, FOMC statement, Texas governor release). CNBC blocked fetching, so I used the Fed's own statement instead.
